data.name: Bahur
data.gender_notes: Bahur is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root word 'b-h-r', meaning 'light, moon'. Bahur is a beautiful Islamic name for a boy, evoking the image of the radiant light of the moon. In Islamic tradition, the moon is a symbol of divine guidance, and a source of peace and tranquility. The name Bahur carries the meaning “Light of the moon” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bahur usually hope their child will grow to embody light of the moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bahur is a name that signifies the beginning of a new day and the hope that comes with it. It is a reminder of the beauty and potential that lies within each day, and the opportunity for growth and renewal.
data.etymology: Bahur belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light of the moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bahur total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: باهور
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من البحر أو النار الشديدة الحرارة
in_arabic.long_meaning: باهور هو اسم يعود إلى الأصول العربية، ويشير إلى البحر أو النار الشديدة الحرارة. وقد ورد ذكره في بعض المصادر العربية القديمة، ويحمل دلالات قوية تتعلق بالقوة والطاقة. يستخدم هذا الاسم في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية لتسمية الأطفال، معبرًا عن الصفات الجيدة مثل الشجاعة والقدرة على التحمل.

in_urdu.name: بہور
in_urdu.meaning: بحر یا شدید گرمی والی ناریسے مشتق نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: بہور ایک عربی ಮೂಲ کا نام ہے جو بحر یا شدید گرمی والی ناریسے مشتق ہے۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں۔ اس نام کا استعمال طفل کی ولادت کے وقت کیا جاتا ہے تاکہ وہ بہادری اور قوت کی صفات کو اپنائے۔

in_hindi.name: बहुर

in_hindi.long_meaning: बहुर एक नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है और इसका अर्थ है बहुत अधिक ऊर्जा या सामर्थ्य रखने वाला। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बच्चों के लिए चुना जाता है, जो उनके व्यक्तित्व में साहस और आत्मविश्वास की विशेषताओं को दर्शाता है।

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar', Volume II, Chapter XLIV: 'Abd al-Rahman I (756-788 AD): The Umayyad Caliphate in Spain (Al-Andalus)
historical_references.context: Bahur ibn Hafsun (d. 796 AD) was a Berber ruler of the Emirate of Seville during the Umayyad Caliphate in Al-Andalus. He succeeded his father Hafsun, who had revolted against the Umayyads and ruled Seville independent from Damascus. Bahur continued his father's resistance against the Umayyads, but was eventually defeated and killed by the Umayyad general, 'Abd al-Rahman I.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Athir's 'Al-Kamel fi al-Tarikh', Volume III: 'The Crusades and the Ayyubids (1100-1250 AD)', under 'Saladin (1137-1193 AD)', 'Bahadur Khan'
historical_references.context: Bahadur Khan was a slave who became a general under Saladin's rule during the Crusades. He was a Kurd from the Jabalqa region and gained fame for his military prowess. In 1175 AD, Bahadur Khan led a successful campaign against the Crusaders in the region of Marqab, which had been in Crusader control for several decades. He was later killed in battle against the Crusaders in 1182 AD.
